cases.prompt: We have a dedicated 16-core Linux box. How do I run AFL++ on all cores against our ./fuzz harness with seeds in seeds/?

any.why: puts the working files on tmpfs

expectations: Runs one primary (-M) and the remaining instances as secondaries (-S), all sharing the same -o output directory.
Runs afl-system-config on the host before the campaign, and warns that it weakens OS security settings so it belongs on a dedicated machine.
Sets AFL_TMPDIR to a tmpfs such as /dev/shm.

cases.prompt: AFL++ is stuck: coverage stops at a chain of magic-value comparisons in our parser. Which compiler mode and options should we use?
expectations: Recommends trying LTO mode (afl-clang-lto) first and falling back to afl-clang-fast if it does not build.
Builds a CMPLOG-instrumented target with AFL_LLVM_CMPLOG=1 and runs an instance with `-c0` (or a CMPLOG binary).
Mentions a dictionary (including AFL++ auto-dictionary from LTO builds) as another way past the magic values.
